_doc: What each case's main.c measures relative to the main.ts every TS runtime runs. same = same algorithm and allocations. suppressed = volatile / noinline / asm deliberately block the optimisation clang would otherwise do, so the c row is a floor for that operation, not for the hardware. different = c does less or other work (lazy split where JS materialises, a hand-written scanner where JS runs a regex engine). libc = the work is delegated to a libc routine with its own algorithm and cost model (regexec, setjmp). hardev/autorun/bench_latest.sh refuses a c row that is not listed here and only pools `same` rows into medianVsCSameProgram. lead = the measured mechanism by which tr does less work than a `same` comparator; a lead over 20% without one is reported as unexplained.

ackermann.lead: tr inlines the self-call one level, which clang does not: more instructions retired, fewer cycles

popcount.why: hand-rolled Kernighan loop, no hardware popcount intrinsic; tr folds the whole loop into a ctpop superinstruction

mandelbrot.why: FMA contraction disabled to match rust rounding

collatz.why: u64 n & 1 and n >>= 1 where main.ts needs f64 % 2 and / 2

generic-id-1m.why: noinline loop_sum keeps the sum out of the push loop

generic-pair-1m.why: the pair never escapes, so it is a local struct; clang is free to reduce the loop

objlit-optional-field-1m.why: the record never escapes, so it is a local struct with a presence flag; clang is free to keep it in registers

split-only-100k.why: materialises the slice array every iteration; tr proves the array is only measured and answers a count
split-only-100k.note: both split operands are literals, so the whole call can be folded at compile time; split-only-argv-100k takes them from argv

split-only-1m.why: materialises the slice array every iteration; tr proves the array is only measured and answers a count
split-only-1m.note: both split operands are literals, so the whole call can be folded at compile time; split-only-argv-100k takes them from argv

split-only-argv-100k.why: materialises the slice array every iteration; tr proves the array is only measured and answers a count

map-str-100k.why: SipHash-1-3 open addressing as std HashMap; tr hashes keys with FNV-1a

dict-count-optional-read-1m.why: FNV-1a open addressing over the 64 keys, as tr's dictionary; the record is a struct with a presence flag

array-copy-1m.why: volatile / asm per element block the memcpy the loop is

array-map-1m.why: noinline callback + volatile keep the call indirect

array-sum-1m.why: volatile / asm per element block vectorisation

array-sum-mixed-1m.why: volatile / asm per element block vectorisation

closure-counter-renamed.why: closure-counter with the captured parameter not spelled like the top-level binding; noinline + volatile forbid devirtualisation

class-method-100k.why: volatile + asm keep both per-iteration heap objects alive

class-method-10m.why: volatile + asm keep both per-iteration heap objects alive

str-concat-ascii-100k.why: volatile + asm keep the per-iteration buffer, which clang would fold

str-concat-ascii-escape-100k.why: the concat is loop-invariant: tr and bun build it once before the loop and store the same string every iteration; main.c mallocs a fresh string every iteration (str-concat-ascii-vary-10m is the case where every runtime must build it)
str-concat-ascii-escape-100k.note: at n=100k bun's work is mostly JIT warm-up (about 690 instructions per iteration against about 24 in steady state), so this ratio favours tr; str-concat-ascii-escape-10m reads the steady state

str-concat-ascii-escape-10m.why: the concat is loop-invariant: tr and bun build it once before the loop and store the same string every iteration; main.c mallocs a fresh string every iteration (str-concat-ascii-vary-10m is the case where every runtime must build it)

str-concat-ascii-vary-10m.why: each result is a fresh malloc buffer of exactly the combined length, stored into an 8-slot ring that frees the slot it replaces, and read back by index

i64-to-str-100k.why: volatile + asm keep each formatted buffer

i64-to-str-10m.why: volatile + asm keep each formatted buffer

json-stringify-100k.why: grows each record buffer from capacity 0 by realloc and escapes the key names at run time; not the fast way to write this in C

rpn-eval-100k.why: lazy in-place tokeniser and a fixed stack array; JS split materialises an array

csv-trim-100k.why: lazy in-place scan; JS split materialises an array

csv-rebuild-100k.why: lazy scan with one malloc per field; JS split materialises an array

throw-catch-100k.why: setjmp / longjmp stands in for throw / catch; macOS setjmp saves the signal mask

regex-dfa-anchored-100k.why: POSIX regcomp / regexec with snprintf input construction

regex-dfa-uflag-100k.why: hand-written utf-8 decode + \p{L} range table; no regex engine

regex-wireback-minlit-100k.why: POSIX regexec; no match array, index or input props

regex-wireback-minlit-10m.why: POSIX regexec; no match array, index or input props

array-any-indexed-100k.why: fixed struct array with a length field where main.ts reads an any[] and dispatches on the tag; clang removes most of the loop (work-only 0.04 ms)

array-any-double-sum-1m.why: double array with no per-element tag where main.ts reads an any[] and dispatches on both operands' tags

array-any-str-to-num-1m.why: char* array with no per-element tag; strtod accepts a different grammar than ToNumber (hex floats, inf / nan spellings); same strings, one conversion per iteration

multibyte-concat-5m.why: uint16_t buffer holds the UTF-16 code units a JS string has; appended in place with doubling capacity from 16 units
multibyte-concat-5m.lead: acc grows through different allocators: tr moves it into a doubled block from its own arena size classes (alloc, copy, free per step), C reallocs through libsystem_malloc. A sample of main.c at 2M rounds puts 75% in realloc / free / malloc and the memmove inside realloc; the same appends into one reused buffer retire 36M instructions / 10M cycles of the program's 269M / 40M, and tr retires 208M / 31M (mini 2026-10-03)

multibyte-concat-flat-5m.why: uint16_t buffer holds the UTF-16 code units a JS string has; appended in place with doubling capacity from 16 units, then the last unit is read
multibyte-concat-flat-5m.lead: the mechanism of multibyte-concat-5m: tr grows acc through its own arena size classes, C reallocs through libsystem_malloc; C 269M instructions / 39M cycles, tr 208M / 31M (mini 2026-10-03)

str-replace-100k.why: hand-coded forward scan for a(b+)c stands in for a regex engine

str-replace-argv-100k.why: hand-coded forward scan for a(b+)c stands in for a regex engine

async-fn-call-100k.why: hand-written microtask queue + reaction list; enqueues and resumes as the spec orders
async-fn-call-100k.caveat: tr's module body waits at these top-level awaits in place: it runs the jobs queued ahead of its continuation on its own stack, in the order the spec gives, and builds no frame for itself

async-suspend-5m.why: hand-written microtask queue + reaction list; step's frame queues its own resumption for the await null and the caller reacts on its still-pending promise, two fifo round trips per call as the spec orders; the yield allocates no promise, since the one the spec creates for null is never observable

promise-all-1m.caveat: tr's module body waits at these top-level awaits in place: it runs the jobs queued ahead of its continuation on its own stack, in the order the spec gives, and builds no frame for itself

promise-await-100k.caveat: tr's module body waits at these top-level awaits in place: it runs the jobs queued ahead of its continuation on its own stack, in the order the spec gives, and builds no frame for itself

promise-chain-1m.caveat: tr's module body waits at these top-level awaits in place: it runs the jobs queued ahead of its continuation on its own stack, in the order the spec gives, and builds no frame for itself

promise-then-100k.caveat: the receiver is Promise.resolve of a number, a fresh fulfilled cell no code has seen: tr's module body runs the then reaction and the await's continuation in place, in the spec's job order, and makes no derived promise (the fused await p.then(f) lane, at its fresh-fulfilled receiver). Sibling with a pending receiver held in a binding: promise-then-pending-100k

promise-then-pending-100k.why: hand-written microtask queue + reaction list; later's frame queues its own resumption for the await null, the then reaction waits in the still-pending promise's list until that resumption settles it, then settles the derived promise the loop reacts on: three fifo round trips per iteration as the spec orders
promise-then-pending-100k.caveat: tr makes no derived promise here (the await is its only reader, so nothing can see it); C allocates and settles one

split-materialize-1m.why: split counts the separators, then allocates one array of pointer-and-length views into the line, no copy per field; rebuilt is appended in place with doubling capacity from 16
split-materialize-1m.lead: with both buffers starting at 16, tr retires 25% fewer instructions (2.05G against 2.72G): 13% is the parts array tr never builds (see caveat), the rest is rebuilt growing 16->32->64 through tr's string free-list pool with no libc call where C reallocs through libsystem_malloc
split-materialize-1m.caveat: tr does not materialise here: parts is only read as parts[k] in order, so the index loop is rewritten into the split iterator and no array exists; siblings: split-materialize-escape-1m, split-materialize-store-1m

split-materialize-escape-1m.why: the slice array of split-materialize-1m, kept alive past its line: each line's array replaces the previous one, which is freed then, and the last is read after the loop; rebuilt is appended in place with doubling capacity from 16

split-materialize-store-1m.why: the slice array of split-materialize-1m stored into a 1024-slot table, each line's array freeing the one it replaces; every table entry is read after the loop; rebuilt is appended in place with doubling capacity from 16

throw-unwind-depth8-1m.why: sigsetjmp / siglongjmp without the signal mask stands in for throw / catch; every frame with a finally has its own jump buffer and re-raises; the thrown object is heap-allocated

str-build-1mb.why: byte buffer appended in place with doubling capacity from 16, a fresh buffer every round

tokenizer-parser-eval-10k.why: tokens stored inline in an array grown by doubling, one malloc per AST node, tree and token array freed per line; the parser state never escapes, so it is a local struct

regex-capture-exec-1m.why: a hand-written matcher for ([a-z]+)=(\d+) stands in for a general regex engine; both captures are written as their own heap strings and the digits parsed with strtoll from the captured one, but only the length of the key is read, so clang removes that allocation

regex-replace-callback-1m.why: a hand-written matcher for ([a-z]+)=(\d+) stands in for a general regex engine; both captures and the replacer's result are their own heap strings, the output is appended in place with doubling capacity from 16
